beare_usage: the transparent — a common nature and power (κοινὴ φύσις καὶ δύναμις) subsisting in all bodies; when actualized by a fiery element it is light; its privation is darkness; colour exists at its limit in determinately bounded bodies.
notes: Central technical term of the treatise; also used in De Anima II.7. The transparent is not peculiar to any element but is a shared property of air, water, and all bodies in varying degrees.

beare_usage: colour — the limit of the transparent in a determinately bounded body; white and black are the extremes, intermediate colours arise by ratio-mixture.
notes: The Pythagoreans named the surface-colour chroia (χρόα), related to but distinguished from chrōma.

beare_usage: sensation, sense-perception — an affection generated in the soul through the medium of the body; the actualization of a sense faculty by its proper object.
notes: Generic term covering all sensory modalities; the treatise's opening establishes that all sensation is a joint function of soul and body.

beare_usage: the common sensibles — figure, magnitude, motion, number; perceived by more than one sense, especially sight and touch. The common sense faculty is numerically one but specifically different for each sense-province.
notes: The doctrine of common sensibles links De Sensu to De Anima III.1-2 on the common sense faculty.

beare_usage: mixture — genuine blending of ingredients at the level of minimal parts, distinguished from juxtaposition (παράθεσις) and superposition (ἐπιπρόσθεσις).
notes: Technical term for genuine blending; Aristotle's preferred mechanism for intermediate colour generation.

beare_usage: potentiality/actuality — applied to perceptibility: sensible qualities exist potentially in sub-threshold magnitudes and become actually perceptible only at sufficient scale. Resolves the puzzle of infinite divisibility of sensible qualities.
notes: The potential/actual distinction is the key to resolving the infinite-divisibility puzzle in ch. 6 and grounding the perceptual threshold doctrine in ch. 7.

beare_usage: light — the colour of the transparent incidentally; the actuality of the transparent qua transparent.
notes: Produced by the presence of a fiery element in the medium.

beare_usage: savour — the affection wrought by the sapid dry in the moist, transforming the sense of taste from potentiality to actuality.
notes: Beare renders 'savour'; could also be 'flavour' or 'juice' (original sense). Seven species paralleling seven species of colour.

beare_usage: odour — analogous to savour but operating through air and water; two species: nutritive (correlated with savours) and pleasant-in-themselves (perceived only by humans).
notes: Central term of ch. 5; smell occupies a middle position between tactual and distance senses.

beare_usage: magnitude — every sensible object is a magnitude; the distance from which it can be perceived is determinate.
juxtaposition — placing white and black side by side in imperceptibly small quantities; rejected hypothesis for colour generation.
notes: One of three hypotheses for intermediate colour generation; rejected in favour of mixture.
